experiments.statusReason: replacement Pod Ready and Deployment back to desired readiness

measurements.name: api_rtt
measurements.label: API request round-trip
measurements.end: KubeScope receives the API server's success response
measurements.description: Client-observed latency of a single API call (network + authn/authz + admission + etcd write). It says nothing about workload readiness.

measurements.name: time_to_replacement_observed
measurements.label: Acknowledged → replacement Pod seen
measurements.end: First watch observation of a Pod with a UID not present before deletion
measurements.description: How long until the ReplicaSet controller's new Pod object was visible to KubeScope (not yet scheduled or running).

measurements.name: time_to_replacement_ready
measurements.label: Acknowledged → replacement Ready
measurements.end: Replacement Pod's Ready condition observed True
measurements.description: Includes scheduling, image pull (often cached), container start and readiness probe period.

measurements.name: time_to_desired_readiness
measurements.label: Acknowledged → desired readiness restored
measurements.end: Deployment converged at baseline desired=2 with replacement Ready
measurements.description: End of the recovery as seen through Deployment status.

measurements.name: recovery_duration
measurements.label: Readiness dip → restored
measurements.start: First observation of readyReplicas below the baseline (2)
measurements.end: Desired readiness restored
measurements.description: Duration ready capacity was observed below baseline. Only measured if a dip was actually observed.

measurements.name: time_to_original_absent
measurements.label: Acknowledged → original Pod gone
measurements.end: Original Pod UID no longer present in the API (watch DELETED or poll 404)
measurements.description: Includes the graceful termination period. Recovery does not wait for this.

timeline.message: Baseline: desired=2 ready=2 available=2 (4 Pods listed)

Expected chain: API server marks the Pod terminating → kubelet stops it → ReplicaSet controller sees too few active Pods and creates a new Pod (new UID) → scheduler binds it → kubelet starts it → readiness probe passes.

gen=20 observedGen=20 spec=2 current=2 updated=2 ready=1 available=1
Replacement Pod reports Ready (readiness probe passing)

Experiment success: replacement Pod Ready and Deployment back to desired readiness

caveats: Timestamps are taken on the KubeScope host when requests return and when watch/poll observations arrive, not inside the control plane.
The replacement is identified as the first demo Pod whose UID was not present before deletion. Another actor creating Pods at the same time could confuse this.
A readiness dip shorter than the watch delivery or poll interval may not be observed.

measurements.description: Client-observed latency of a single API call (network + authn/authz + admission + etcd write). It says nothing about workload readiness.

measurements.name: time_to_convergence
measurements.label: Acknowledged → converged
measurements.start: PATCH acknowledged by the API server
measurements.end: First observation with observedGeneration ≥ patched generation and updated = ready = available = status.replicas = desired
measurements.description: Includes controller reconciliation, scheduling, image pulls, container start, readiness probes and watch/poll delivery to KubeScope. Not a pure control-plane latency.

measurements.name: end_to_end
measurements.label: Request start → converged
measurements.end: Convergence observed
measurements.description: api_rtt + time_to_convergence.

timeline.message: Expected chain: API server persists spec.replicas=2 → Deployment controller resizes the ReplicaSet → ReplicaSet controller creates/deletes Pods → scheduler binds new Pods → kubelet starts containers → readiness probe passes.
PATCH acknowledged in 2 ms: generation=20 resourceVersion=2299
gen=20 observedGen=20 spec=2 current=4 updated=4 ready=4 available=4
Normal ScalingReplicaSet (deployment-controller): Scaled down replica set demo-api-56df899bbf from 4 to 2
gen=20 observedGen=20 spec=2 current=2 updated=2 ready=2 available=2
Experiment success: Deployment converged to 2 ready/available replicas

caveats: Timestamps are taken on the KubeScope host when requests return and when watch/poll observations arrive, not inside the control plane.
Time-to-convergence includes scheduling, image pulls, container start-up and readiness probes; it is not control-plane latency.
Polling every 2s backs up the watch, so convergence can be detected up to one watch-delivery or poll interval late.
